Euro slides to fresh lows against US dollar and British pound despite ECB rate hikes
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-15
12:25:34 UTC
21:25:34 KST

The euro slid this week to its weakest level against the US dollar since mid-May 2025 and the British pound since early June 2025, as an energy shock, France’s debt crisis and a resurgent US dollar outweigh two interest rate hikes by the European Central Bank.
Europe’s single currency fell on Wednesday to lows against the US dollar not seen since mid-May last year, and against the British pound since early June last year, as soaring energy costs, a bond market revolt over French public finances and a stronger US dollar weigh on it.
The slide comes even though the European Central Bank (ECB) has raised interest rates twice this year, which would normally support a currency.
The euro traded at roughly $1.111 on Wednesday, its weakest since mid-May 2025 and below the low it first hit earlier this month, before rebounding slightly to around $1.121 in early trading on Thursday.
It is down more than 5% since late August, completely reversing the recovery it staged over the summer.
Against the British pound, it hit roughly £0.842 on Wednesday, the lowest since early June 2025, and edged back to around £0.846 on Thursday. That leaves it down roughly 2% since late September, wiping out the gains it had made since mid-July.
An exchange rate has two sides, so the euro’s slide also reflects a stronger US dollar.
The US dollar index, which tracks it against major currencies, hit an 18-month high on Wednesday after US inflation rose to 3.7% in September, above forecasts.
Rate hikes offer no shield
The US inflation data roughly doubled traders’ bets that the Federal Reserve will raise rates on 28 October. Its benchmark rate already stands at 3.75-4%, well above the ECB’s current 2.5%.
The ECB raised its deposit rate by a quarter point to 2.5% on 10 September, its second hike this year, to counter the energy shock from the Iran war as Europe imports most of its energy, leaving it more exposed to the oil price spike than the US.
Eurozone inflation has since climbed to 3.8%, a three-year high.
Traders are currently betting the ECB will keep rates on hold on 29 October before raising them again in December.
"We are probably going to have to hike again," Belgian central bank governor Pierre Wunsch told Bloomberg on Wednesday.
Bundesbank president Joachim Nagel struck a more patient tone, saying earlier this month that "there are so far no clear signs that inflation has fed through to price and wage setting."
In the UK, robust economic data has fuelled bets that the Bank of England will also raise rates in November, supporting the British pound.
French debt crisis
The extra yield investors demand to hold French rather than German 10-year debt, a gauge of nerves, rose above 150 basis points earlier this month, the most since the euro debt crisis around 2011.
The French government’s 2027 budget, which aims to save some €54 billion and narrow the deficit to 5% of economic output from an expected 5.4% this year, faces a rocky ride through a divided parliament, where debate began on Tuesday amid student protests revindicating additional public funding for the education system.
France's public debt reached a record 119% of GDP at the end of June 2026, according to INSEE data. This represents about €3.59 trillion and is double the official EU threshold for public debt-to-GDP which is 60%.
ECB President Christine Lagarde has dampened hopes of the central bank helping.
"The primary and first solution lies at home in France [...] and it has to do with fiscal policies," Lagarde stated on Wednesday on the sidelines of the annual meeting of the IMF and the World Bank Group in Bangkok.
Spain, meanwhile, heads to a snap election on 29 November, adding to the political turmoil that is rattling European markets.
Investors will next look to final eurozone inflation figures on Friday, followed by interest rate decisions from the Federal Reserve on 28 October and the ECB a day later.

At the invitation of Prime Minister of the Republic of Uzbekistan Abdulla Aripov, Premier of the State Council Li Qiang will pay an official visit to Uzbekistan from October 17 to 18.
At the invitation of Prime Minister of the Republic of Tajikistan Kokhir Rasulzoda, Premier Li Qiang will pay an official visit to Tajikistan from October 18 to 20 and attend the 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO).
At the invitation of Prime Minister of the Russian Federation Mikhail Mishustin, Premier Li Qiang will travel to Russia from October 20 to 22 for the 31st regular meeting between Chinese and Russian heads of government.
Xinhua News Agency: You just announced that Premier Li Qiang will visit Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, and attend the 25th meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization. He will also travel to Russia for the 31st regular meeting between Chinese and Russian heads of government. Can you share the background and China’s expectation?
Mao Ning: China and Uzbekistan are all-weather comprehensive strategic partners for the new era. Over recent years, under the strategic guidance of President Xi Jinping and President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, China-Uzbekistan relations have entered a golden period with stronger mutual trust and fruitful cooperation in various areas. In August this year, the two presidents met in Bishkek where they made new strategic planning for the future development of bilateral relations. China and Tajikistan are friendly neighbors and comprehensive strategic cooperative partners for the new era. Since the two countries established diplomatic relations, bilateral ties have maintained a sound and steady momentum of growth. In May this year, President Xi Jinping met with President Emomali Rahmon who was on a state visit to China. The two sides signed and issued the treaty on permanent good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation, providing a firm safeguard for the ever-lasting friendship between the two countries. China hopes the visit will galvanize efforts of all three countries to accelerate the implementation of the important common understandings between the presidents, deepen political mutual trust, expand mutually-beneficial cooperation, promote common development, and provide new impetus for building the China-Uzbekistan and China-Tajikistan community with a shared future.
This year marks the 30th anniversary of the China-Russia strategic partnership of coordination and the 25th anniversary of the signing of the China-Russia Treaty of Good-Neighborliness and Friendly Cooperation. President Xi Jinping and President Vladimir Putin have met twice this year, guiding bilateral relations into a new stage with higher-quality and faster development. Premier Li Qiang’s attendance at the 31st regular meeting between Chinese and Russian heads of government will serve as an opportunity for the two countries to work together to deliver on the important common understandings between the two presidents, deepen political mutual trust, and enhance and substantiate all-round practical cooperation for the benefit of the two peoples.
The SCO is in its 25th year now. At the successful SCO Summit in Bishkek not long ago, leaders of member states reached important common understandings on carrying forward the Shanghai Spirit under the new circumstances, promoting SCO’s development and cooperation, and improving the global governance system. President Xi Jinping made an in-depth elaboration on the core tenets of an equal and orderly multipolar world, put forward new initiatives on practical cooperation, and charted the course for high-quality development of the SCO. At the upcoming meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of the SCO in Dushanbe, Premier Li Qiang will have in-depth exchanges of views with various parties on implementing the strategic blueprint of the SCO Tianjin Summit and the outcome consensus of the SCO Bishkek Summit, so as to better protect the shared interests of member states and make SCO’s contribution to peace, stability, development and prosperity of the region and beyond.
Bloomberg: Can you confirm a report that China has agreed to restructure some of Zimbabwe’s debt? This is according to Zimbabwe’s finance minister, but we haven’t heard anything about this from China.
Mao Ning: China and Zimbabwe are traditional friends. The Chinese side attaches high importance to Zimbabwe’s debt treatment request. The competent authorities and financial institutions of both sides are in communication over this. For more updates, I would refer you to the competent Chinese authorities.

Is it the same as Russia’s position?
Mao Ning: We have released a readout on the meeting between Foreign Minister Wang Yi and his Russian counterpart. I don’t have anything further to add.
Global Times: Japanese media recently disclosed for the first time internal meeting minutes of the Yasukuni war shrine revealing the decision-making process of the enshrinement of 14 Class-A war criminals including Hideki Tojo. It shows that the Japanese government made arrangements on the enshrinement of Class-A war criminals with the shrine in as early as the 1960s, but chose to keep the public in the dark until it was revealed in 1979. What’s China’s comment?

These Class-A war criminals were the chief culprits behind Japanese militarists’ war of aggression with the blood of innumerable war victims on their hands. The solemn verdict of the Tokyo Trials condemned them to perpetual infamy, thereby upholding international justice and laying the legal foundation for the postwar international order. Yet those running the Japanese government have again and again paid respects to what is in fact a shrine to war criminals. One has to ask: where has the conscience gone?
History shall not be rewritten. Truth shall not be erased. Japan committed undeniable crimes during its militarist aggression. Those running the Japanese government must face history squarely, reflect on the war crimes, and make a genuine break with its militarist past.

Türkiye expects the United States to lift CAATSA sanctions and all restrictions on its defence industry as talks continue over the delivery of six F-35 fighter jets produced for Ankara, the Turkish National Defence Ministry said on Thursday.
“Our expectation is the lifting of CAATSA sanctions, which are incompatible with the spirit of alliance, and all direct or indirect restrictions on our defence industry,” ministry spokesperson Zeki Akturk said, referring to the Countering America’s Adversaries Through Sanctions Act.
The ministry said contacts with US officials were continuing and expressed hope for a positive outcome in line with the two countries’ alliance ties and mutual interests.
Türkiye outlines potential Saudi military role
Akturk said any Turkish military contribution to Saudi Arabia under the new Mecca Defence Alliance would be determined in accordance with Türkiye’s Constitution and relevant legislation.
The agreement, signed in August by Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, requires parliamentary approval and completion of the procedures for deploying Turkish Armed Forces personnel abroad.
Any contribution would depend on Saudi Arabia’s needs, developments on the ground and operational requirements, he said.
